Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a January 2028 personal-practice log for my established weekly routine. Use the routine's established day of the week and create a separate dated entry for every occurrence of that day in January. Include fields for subject, materials, technique notes, completion, and storage. Make sure the setup fits the current household cadence. Save it as a document.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "January 2028 Watercolor Personal-Practice Log", "body": "# January 2028 Watercolor Personal-Practice Log

**Routine:** Sunday watercolor at the Cherrywood painting corner; keep the usual roughly two-hour, low-pressure personal block. This log does not assign a new start time or turn the session into a finished-work commitment.

**Household fit:** Keep Sunday painting separate from Sam’s fixed Monday no-service/shared-time block (6:30–9:30pm). Sunday remains flexible; no missed session is owed or moved into Monday. Use the dedicated painting corner and its normal supplies rather than taking over shared household surfaces. These are personal studies, with no sale, exhibition, or demonstration commitment.

**Usual kit:** 9 × 12 in, 140-lb cold-press watercolor paper; board; palette; brushes; ultramarine, burnt sienna, and yellow ochre; two water jars; towel. Use the existing Cherrywood window light, turned board orientation to avoid glare.

---

## Sunday, January 2
- **Subject:** Winter kitchen-window still life; choose one simple object or small grouping.
- **Materials:** Usual kit; one 9 × 12 in sheet.
- **Technique notes:** Begin with a three-value thumbnail. Keep the first wash transparent; distinguish cool window shadow from a restrained warm edge by value, not extra saturation. Preserve the lightest shape and stop before repeated corrections muddy it.
- **Completion:** ☐ Not yet  ☐ Complete  ☐ Partial — notes: __________
- **Storage:** Let dry flat, face up, in the dedicated dry zone. Once fully dry, store flat in the private watercolor portfolio. Actual location/date: __________

## Sunday, January 9
- **Subject:** Crumpled silver gift ribbon on brown kraft paper (continue the December study motif; simplify to a few large folds).
- **Materials:** Usual kit; one 9 × 12 in sheet; scrap for a cool-neutral test.
- **Technique notes:** Map light, midtone, and dark masses first; reserve paper highlights. Mix a restrained cool neutral with ultramarine and burnt sienna, testing before the sheet. Use a few crisp highlight boundaries against softer reflected shadows; omit tiny reflections.
- **Completion:** ☐ Not yet  ☐ Complete  ☐ Partial — notes: __________
- **Storage:** Let dry flat, face up, in the dedicated dry zone. Once fully dry, store flat in the private watercolor portfolio. Actual location/date: __________

## Sunday, January 16
- **Subject:** A glass jar or bottle in Cherrywood window light.
- **Materials:** Usual kit; one 9 × 12 in sheet.
- **Technique notes:** Reserve the window highlight. Establish a broad cool shadow wash first and let it dry before adding limited darker accents. Keep the warm reflected edge subtle through value separation; avoid repainting the highlight.
- **Completion:** ☐ Not yet  ☐ Complete  ☐ Partial — notes: __________
- **Storage:** Let dry flat, face up, in the dedicated dry zone. Once fully dry, store flat in the private watercolor portfolio. Actual location/date: __________

## Sunday, January 23
- **Subject:** Small rainy-doorway or street-corner study, from a remembered view or personal reference.
- **Materials:** Usual kit; one 9 × 12 in sheet; timer; scrap paper.
- **Technique notes:** Keep the cool street wash and warm doorway edge distinct. Use the established blue-plus-brown mix and consistent brush load; test a single dark-rain interruption around the useful 5½-minute window, changing no other variable. Stop after the planned mark rather than re-entering as the sheen fades.
- **Completion:** ☐ Not yet  ☐ Complete  ☐ Partial — notes: __________
- **Storage:** Let dry flat, face up, in the dedicated dry zone. Once fully dry, store flat in the private watercolor portfolio. Actual location/date: __________

## Sunday, January 30
- **Subject:** Kibo in a quiet window-shadow or warm-floor-light arrangement, if he settles; otherwise use a nearby household still life.
- **Materials:** Usual kit; one 9 × 12 in sheet.
- **Technique notes:** Plan three values and the focal shape before painting. Keep the largest shadow transparent, use soft and lost edges for surrounding forms, and save only a few hard edges for structure. Avoid chasing facial detail; stop when the light/shadow read is clear.
- **Completion:** ☐ Not yet  ☐ Complete  ☐ Partial — notes: __________
- **Storage:** Let dry flat, face up, in the dedicated dry zone. Once fully dry, store flat in the private watercolor portfolio. Actual location/date: __________

It must not substitute other weekly dates or omit any of these five dates.

The document clearly identifies the logged personal practice as watercolor painting. Mentioning watercolor anywhere in the document body is sufficient; it need not be repeated in every entry.

Each of the five dated weekly entries provides usable fields or prompts for all of the following: subject, materials, technique notes, completion status, and storage or storage location.

The document frames the Sunday watercolor entries as a flexible, separate personal practice rather than protected or mandatory appointments. Equivalent wording passes if it conveys that Sunday or the painting practice remains flexible and keeps watercolor separate from household shared-time, relationship-maintenance, make-up-time, or work obligations; an explicit reference to restaurant needs is not required.
